cards.answer: Aphelios is a basic-attack-focused marksman who deals mainly physical damage. He equips two of five weapons, each with distinct attacks and an ability determined by his main-hand weapon. Severum's Onslaught grants movement speed, but he has no dash or blink, making positioning important when enemies close in.
cards.counterplay: Assess both weapons before approaching and look for opportunities to close the distance.

cards.answer: Aphelios equips two of five weapons with distinct attacks and abilities; the main-hand determines his active, and weapon actives have separate cooldowns. Basic attacks and weapon-active casts spend ammunition, but automatic attacks caused by abilities spend no additional ammunition; an empty weapon moves to the queue's end and is replaced by the next reserve weapon. He starts with Calibrum main-hand and Severum off-hand, then Gravitum, Infernum and Crescendum in reserve; E shows the next weapon and can display a text prompt. Phase is available from the start, weapon actives unlock at level 2, and Moonlight Vigil unlocks at level 6 and improves at levels 11 and 16; skill points grant attack damage, attack speed or lethality instead of ability ranks.
cards.counterplay: Track his weapon pair and ammunition; a swap may give him another available active.

Calibrum hits through abilities mark enemies for a long-range follow-up with the off-hand weapon, or the main-hand weapon if Calibrum is off-hand. The follow-up consumes all marks and adds physical damage for each mark consumed.
cards.counterplay: Respect marked follow-ups even outside his ordinary attack range.

cards.answer: Crescendum must return before Aphelios can attack again, and catching it resets his attack timer, favoring close-range attacks with shorter return travel. Abilities that would attack with Crescendum instead send returning mirror chakrams; catching them strengthens Crescendum attacks with bonus physical damage based on how many he holds. Catching another mirror chakram or attacking a champion with Crescendum refreshes their duration.
cards.counterplay: Keep your distance and disengage from accumulated chakrams to let their temporary strength expire.

Aphelios accumulates the Chakrams he catches, up to 20, which last for 5 seconds or until Crescendum is depleted of Moonlight.
Other abilities will create mirror chakrams that he gathers, and his basic attacks deal bonus physical damage based on how many mirror chakrams he holds.

cards.answer: Moonlight Vigil explodes on an enemy champion, deals physical damage to champions in the area, then follows with physical attacks carrying the main-hand weapon's effect chosen when fired; swapping during flight does not change it. Calibrum applies empowered marks; Severum heals Aphelios through the blast and follow-up attacks; Gravitum applies an enhanced slow and lets Binding Eclipse root affected targets for longer. cards.counterplay: Assess his main-hand weapon when he fires; spread out against Infernum and respect Crescendum's strengthened attacks afterward.
